bullets: CRL broadcast footage with Ryley's voice-over, video 1103.1s-1371.2s (no readable match clock; all times are video seconds). He names the deck himself: "this is my favorite deck of all time and I was telling you guys that this deck is back after the addition of the Evo Princess... I'm playing Mighty Miner Bait in competitive" (1141-1157s). Result: win by concession - "he actually ended up giving up. So I was in a 1-0 lead in the duel for the qualification" (1365-1368s), against Lucas on a Miner / Magic Archer / Royal Delivery control list.

Pilots it as a patient bait deck, not a rush: "I was just playing very passive, kind of trusting my defense, and knowing that I can outcycle him with the delivery throughout the game, just kind of get some nice damage" (1231-1238s). Goblin Barrels only go out when the opponent's Royal Delivery is counted out of cycle (t=1319.3, t=1341.8; "I went for the barrel cuz I outcycled the delivery", 1349-1350s).

Cycle discipline governs the defence: he refuses to lay the Cannon while Ice Spirit is out of cycle - "you guys may be wondering why I deny cannon... That is because I didn't have my ice spirit in cycle" (1159-1163s) - and when he does play the Evo Cannon he plays it immediately for the deploy barrage (t=1240.2, "I hit everything right there with that cannon", 1245-1248s).

The win comes from accumulated Princess presence plus the Rocket, not from one push: Princess placements at (9, 11), (8, 12), (8, 12), (8, 13) and (8, 2) over t=1223-1360, and "there was no way that he was going to be able to come back from the rocket cycle and the princess stack just having two princess on the board" (1358-1363s).

Mighty Miner is the deck's flex slot: a bridge play to force the opponent's Magic Archer (t=1304.3, "I mighty mined the bridge knowing he had to go for the magic cartridge", 1307-1309s) and a repeat Miner catcher on defence (t=1224.2, t=1332.3, t=1356.4; "I caught the miner again, just over and over again somehow", 1345-1346s).

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel and Princess are both Log/Arrows bait played behind cheap cycle cards, and the game plan Ryley states is to outcycle the opponent's single Goblin Barrel answer rather than to build a push.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Classic Log Bait: Goblin Barrel and Princess force the opponent to spend their small spell, and once it is spent the other threat gets through for free. Ryley's version swaps the usual mini-tank for a Mighty Miner, which gives the deck both a bridge play that forces out enemy support ("I mighty mined the bridge knowing he had to go for the magic cartridge", 1307-1309s) and a reliable answer to Miner and tanky ground units on defence. Cannon, Skeletons, Ice Spirit and The Log are the whole defence, so the deck is cycle-dependent by design - Ryley refuses to lay the Cannon when Ice Spirit is out of cycle (1159-1172s), and gates every Goblin Barrel on having counted the opponent's answer out of hand (1322-1350s). Rocket is the closer, used both as real damage and as a hovered bluff (1310-1320s), and the evolved Princess is what he says brought the deck back into competitive play (1145-1150s).
